claims.statement: Mazdutide is a long-acting synthetic oxyntomodulin analog that acts as a dual agonist at the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) and the glucagon receptor (GCGR), stimulating insulin secretion and engaging glucagon-receptor-mediated energy expenditure pathways alongside GLP-1 receptor activity.

By targeting the GCG receptor, Lilly and Innovent figure mazdutide should help increase the body's energy expenditure, spurring changes in the liver, brain and white and brown adipose tissue that complement the reduced energy intake triggered by GLP-1 activation.

claims.statement: In GLORY-1, a randomized, controlled phase 3 trial in 610 Chinese adults with obesity or overweight-plus-comorbidity, once-weekly mazdutide produced a mean body-weight change at 48 weeks of -11.00% (4 mg) and -14.01% (6 mg) versus a 0.30% increase with placebo, per an independent physician review of the published NEJM data; the sponsor's press release separately reported -12.05% (4 mg), -14.84% (6 mg), and -0.47% for placebo, a discrepancy not yet resolved against the NEJM primary full text. A press-release-only figure that 50.6% of participants on 6 mg achieved ≥15% weight loss versus 2.1% on placebo has not been independently corroborated this session and should be treated with the same caution as the disputed percentages.

needs-adjustment-remediation-2026-08-29 (session 2): fetched and verbatim-quoted an independent physician-review commentary (gutsandgrowth.com) analyzing the published NEJM GLORY-1 data. It reports week-48 figures of -11.00% (4mg), -14.01% (6mg), and +0.30% (placebo) -- agreeing with the prior Semantic Scholar pull on the 6mg/placebo values and disagreeing with the sponsor press release (-12.05%, -14.84%, -0.47%).
